introduction_markdown:
Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board, Ordinary Level Examination, June 2020. Chemistry, Paper 2 (subject code 0515). Duration: two and a half hours.

This paper is arranged in three sections, A, B and C. Section A: attempt ALL 5 questions; you will be graded for the best 4 questions answered. Section B: answer BOTH questions in this section. Section C: answer 2 questions out of 3.

In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Non-programmable calculators are allowed. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

**Useful data:** relative atomic masses H = 1.0, C = 12.0, O = 16.0, Cu = 64.0; 1 faraday = 96000 coulombs; molar volume of a gas at r.t.p. = 24000 cm$^3$; specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 J g$^{-1}$ $^\circ$C$^{-1}$; Avogadro number = $6.02\times10^{23}$; $0^\circ$C = 273 K.
enonce_intro_markdown:
This question concerns the following table showing the composition of some atoms.

| Atoms | Atomic Number | Mass Number |
|---|---|---|
| W | 6 | 12 |
| X | 9 | 19 |
| Y | 11 | 23 |
| Z | 16 | 32 |
incertitudes: Les atomes W, X, Y, Z sont donnes par des lettres : le corrige indique entre parentheses leur identite reelle (C, F, Na, S) sans l'imposer a l'eleve.

Regle de choix de la Section A : l'en-tete dit « ATTEMPT ALL 5 questions. You will be graded for the best 4 », le titre de la section dit « Answer ALL questions ». Les deux sont compatibles ; la regle est codee « 4 sur 5 » (les 4 meilleures comptent), tous les exercices restant a traiter.
Le filigrane (gcerevision.com) et des annotations manuscrites parasites sont ignores ; les pages portent aussi des traces de transparence (texte inverse du verso), sans effet sur la lecture.

questions.enonce_markdown: How many electrons and neutrons are found in the atom X? *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
For atom X: atomic number = 9, mass number = 19.

- Electrons = atomic number (a neutral atom) = **9**.
- Neutrons = mass number - atomic number = $19 - 9 =$ **10**.

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify an atom of a metal from W, X, Y, Z. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: **Y.** Its atomic number is 11, so its electronic configuration is 2, 8, 1: it has one electron in its outer shell, which it loses easily to form a positive ion, as metals do. (Y is sodium; W, X and Z, with 4, 7 and 6 outer electrons, are non-metals: carbon, fluorine and sulphur.)

questions.enonce_markdown: Write the electronic configuration of Z. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: Z has atomic number 16, so 16 electrons: **2, 8, 6**.

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the bond type and formula of a compound formed between W and X. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
- W (2, 4) has 4 outer electrons and X (2, 7) has 7 outer electrons: both are non-metals, so they **share** electrons.
- **Bond type: covalent bond.**
- W needs 4 more electrons and each X needs only 1, so one W atom combines with four X atoms.
- **Formula: $\mathrm{WX_4}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Y forms a basic oxide.

(i) Write the formula of the oxide.

(ii) Write an equation to show the reaction of the oxide with water. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) Y has one outer electron, so it forms the ion $\mathrm{Y^+}$; oxygen forms $\mathrm{O^{2-}}$. The oxide is **$\mathrm{Y_2O}$**.

(ii) The basic oxide dissolves in water to give the hydroxide (an alkali):

$\mathrm{Y_2O} + \mathrm{H_2O} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{YOH}$

(Balance check: Y 2 = 2, O 2 = 2, H 2 = 2. For sodium this is $\mathrm{Na_2O} + \mathrm{H_2O} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{NaOH}$.)

questions.enonce_markdown: To which group of the periodic table would the element Z be classified? Give an explanation. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown: **Group VI** (Group 16). Z has the electronic configuration 2, 8, 6: it has **6 electrons in its outer shell**, and the group number of a main-group element equals its number of outer electrons.
